one_month_reasoning: DOCN's Q3 2026 report is expected Nov 3-5 (source 19), i.e. just after the window closes (Nov 1 is a Sunday; the last close in the window is Oct 30), so the company's own catalyst most likely falls outside it. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 prints (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META, late October) with capex and AI-capacity commentary, which moves the neocloud group (CRWV, NBIS, IREN), and DOCN has traded with that group. The group's September de-rating came from capex/financing worries rather than demand, so hyperscaler capex raises are a two-sided risk (bullish for demand, bearish for financing). I see no edge, so the distribution is centered just below spot ($139, a slight discount for post-run-up mean reversion after the drop from $187) with monthly sigma ~22.5% (82%/sqrt(12)~23.7%, trimmed slightly). Risk: if earnings land on or before Oct 30, the variance would be larger.

fair_value.method: Blend of 45x CY2028E EPS of $2.40 (~$108) and a 10-year DCF (11% WACC, 4% terminal, revenue +50% in 2027 fading to 8%, FCF margin to 22%) rolled forward 12 months (~$102). Both sit below the $140 price, which is 78x CY2027 consensus EPS.

bear.story: AI ARR growth slows as GPU rental prices roll over (H200 already -7.5% m/m) and larger neoclouds/hyperscalers undercut inference pricing. 2027 growth lands at 30-35% vs the >50% target, capex and finance leases strain FCF, and further equity/convert issuance dilutes holders. The multiple compresses to ~35x a lower ~$1.85 2028 EPS.

base.story: Industry demand stays capacity-constrained through 2027 (hyperscaler capex ~$1T, CRWV backlog $104B, Akamai GPUs sold out), so DOCN delivers roughly 45-50% growth. EPS growth is muted by depreciation, and the multiple de-rates from 78x to ~55x CY2028 EPS of ~$2.45, leaving the stock near flat.

bull.story: Inference is the growth vector and DOCN's developer/SMB inference platform compounds (inference +~800% y/y, $1M+ customer ARR +214%). 2027 growth exceeds 60% with margins stable, the market keeps a premium AI-growth multiple (~75x on ~$3.2 2028 EPS), and the stock re-tests and breaks the $187 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: Calendar-2027 P/E (CY2027 consensus EPS; non-calendar FYs calendarized as noted) across 11 profitable peers: 14.5x (ORCL) to 209x (NET), median 41.0x (FSLY), interquartile ~23x-94x. CRWV and NBIS are loss-making on CY2027 (n/m). A consistent CY2027 EBITDA consensus was not accessible for the peers, so forward EV/EBITDA is left null rather than mixing bases. For DOCN, my own ~$0.62B 2027 adj EBITDA (mgmt >50% growth x ~35% margin) gives ~28x EV/CY2027 EBITDA on a $17.7B EV.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: We apply 45x CY2028E EPS, slightly above the 41x CY2027 peer median and well inside the range. DOCN trades at 78x CY2027 EPS, roughly the 70th-80th percentile of the peer set.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A small premium to the median is justified because DOCN's CY2027 EPS growth (22%, likely ~30-35% in 2028) and revenue growth (>50% per mgmt, RPO $894M up 12x) are structurally above the peer median EPS growth of ~20%. A full high-growth software multiple (NET/SNOW/DDOG at 94-209x) is not justified: DOCN's AI growth is capex- and lease-funded with gross margin falling (60%->55%), EPS growth lags revenue growth, and the comparable capital-intensive GPU clouds (CRWV, NBIS, ORCL) trade at n/m or 14.5x on earnings. The September neocloud de-rating shows the market will not pay software multiples for capex-heavy growth.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$75 (roughly 40x CY2027 EPS and under half the August high), the price would most likely reflect a fundamental break rather than volatility: AI customer ARR deceleration, a guide-down from the >50% 2027 growth target, GPU rental price deflation hitting DOCN's AI pricing, or a dilutive financing to fund capex/finance leases. The core (non-AI) cloud plus a modest AI business is worth roughly $70-80 on peer-median multiples.

key_uncertainties: Whether AI inference growth (+~800% y/y) persists, or GPU-hour pricing deflates as Blackwell supply expands and hyperscalers and new entrants (Meta, SpaceX) add capacity
Capital intensity: $2.8B uncommenced data-center leases and $578M finance leases versus FCF; risk of further equity or convertible issuance
Gross-margin path (60%->55% in H1-26) and how much revenue growth reaches EPS
Neocloud sector multiple and financing sentiment, which drove the September selloff independent of DOCN fundamentals
Server DRAM/component inflation (+13-18% q/q in Q3) raising unit costs for non-hyperscale buyers like DOCN
reasoning: Company facts: Q2-26 revenue $281M (+29%), AI customer ARR $234M (+212%), RPO $894M (12x), FY26 guide $1.17-1.18B revenue and $1.35-1.40 EPS, Q3 EPS guide stepping down to $0.28-0.30 because of AI capacity costs, and mgmt targeting >50% growth in 2027. Industry lane: demand evidence is strong across the chain. CoreWeave revenue +112% with a $104B backlog and managed inference ARR above $100M, Akamai's cloud infrastructure +39% with GPUs sold out and a $600M robotics deal, Citi/Moody's see ~$0.8-1T of 2027 hyperscaler capex, and GPU rental indices rose ~12% m/m for H100/B200 in September (H200 -7.5%). Against that, the neocloud group de-rated sharply in Aug-Sep on capex/financing intensity and new entrants, memory prices are inflating component costs, and DOCN's own gross margin is compressing. Valuation: at $140 DOCN trades at 78x CY2027 consensus EPS vs a 41x CY2027 peer median (consistent calendar-2027 basis, 13 peers), and my P/E and DCF methods give ~$102-108, so fundamentals argue for downside drift. Momentum, a ~$175 sell-side average target and a clearly favourable industry demand backdrop argue the market will keep paying for growth. I set the 12-month median at ~$132 (below spot, above fair value) with a wide, fat-tailed lognormal mix (sigma 0.62/0.80, vs 82% realized), giving P(>=140) ~47%, P(>=210) ~25% and P(>=70) ~82%. Research was limited: Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage estimates were unavailable (plan/rate limits), several pages blocked fetching (Invezz, DCD, Zacks), and peer forward EBITDA could not be sourced on a consistent basis.
